notes.title: Roadmap & Upcoming Update
notes.notes: [p]Hello Explorers,[/p][p]It’s been a while since our last update, and we wanted to share some honest news with you about the state of Wild Planet and where we’re headed next.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/667838d641f6b5052e11139a73085c0c3c689c2a.png"][/img][/p][p]Since the last patch, things have been a bit quieter on our side. The financial situation after losing our publishing partnership hasn’t been ideal, and it limited our ability to push development at full force. Despite this, we’ve kept working in the background and reshaping the project to ensure it stays sustainable while still delivering the core vision we believe in.[/p][p]As part of this rescope, we’ve had to make some tough choices: three biomes that were initially planned are now removed from the roadmap. The final game will feature six biomes in total still plenty of variety and exploration, but with a tighter focus that allows us to polish each one properly.[/p][p]We are also reworking and removing some features that didn’t quite fit, while adding new systems and mechanics that should make the overall gameplay smoother, more rewarding, and fun. Our goal is quality over quantity, and this adjustment will help us reach that.[/p][p]We know news has been sparse lately, and we’re sorry for the silence. We didn’t want to share half-formed promises instead, we’ve been preparing for the next update, which we want to bring with proper new content you can actually play and enjoy.[/p][p]To give you a better picture, here’s what’s coming up:[/p][p][b]A general roadmap of the next phases of development is being polished and will be posted publicly for anyone interested.[/b][/p][p]A few sneak peeks into the upcoming content and systems we’re working on while preparing the next update, we’ve been working on a lot of concept art and prototypes [/p][list][*][p][b]Tier 3 Technology & Benches[/b] – early sketches and WIP models for advanced crafting stations, unlocking new possibilities in late-game progression.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/27aa84c6da888630a7b5a1060522deec25d2a43a.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][b]Base Building Concepts[/b] – experimenting with fresh structures and layouts to give more freedom and creativity when expanding your base.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/cb8d4080b664e31416f967e36d764798de03e9c7.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][b]Biome Research & Maps[/b] – refining the identity, resources, and exploration flow of the 6 final biomes.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/af2376c29b46c5d4961216eb472359ce64ea2d7c.png"][/img][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/a91470514ce59596d112c0c4392c76c5208140a3.png"][/img][/p][/*][*][p][b]New Dungeons[/b] – we’re designing deeper, more atmospheric dungeons with unique challenges, rewards, and lore pieces to uncover.[/p][p][/p][/*][/list][p]These are still in development, but we wanted to share a small glimpse at how the world and its systems are evolving behind the curtain.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you so much for your patience and support. Wild Planet is still alive and moving forward just at a slightly different pace than we first envisioned. We can’t wait to show you more very soon.[/p][p][/p][p]Stay tuned,[/p][p]The Wild Planet Team[/p]

notes.title: Sands of Renewal - Content Update
notes.notes:
[h1]Wild Planet Early Access 1.2.0.0 - Sands of renewal[/h1]

Greetings, explorers!

We’re back with a massive content update for Wild Planet! Early Access 1.2.0.0 brings a huge overhaul to the Desert Biome, new areas to discover, and a host of improvements to the survival experience. Let’s dive into what’s new!

We’re trying something new this time with a short trailer showcasing the latest update! Check out the Canyon Biome, the revamped Desert, and more.

[previewyoutube=eE120Ak9Q9k;full][/previewyoutube]

Do you like these videos? Should we keep making them? Let us know!

[h2]New Content & Biome Overhaul[/h2]

[h3]Canyon Biome (New!)[/h3]
We’ve added a brand-new Canyon Biome, offering a glimpse of what’s to come. This rugged landscape is located on the edge of the Field Biome and serves as a transition zone for future expansions.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/66d2298d5f3a5554b01ac2b7062b446a1c7cbd7a.png[/img]

[h3]Desert Biome Revamp[/h3]
[list]
[*] The Desert Biome has been completely redone from the ground up
[*] New Oasis Area  A lush reprieve in the arid wasteland, full of valuable resources.
[*] New Desert Trees More variety in the environment for better immersion.
[*] New Plasma Field Area  A new area to farm plasma with your drills
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/74bfdfeaf9b0fd080cdfdb4384218c57aabf0ee3.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/117e3612438ffd8f697f3a924bfef285f514d686.png[/img]

[h2]Dungeon Overhaul[/h2]
[h3]Crashed Ship Dungeon (Forest)[/h3] A full remake with improved level design, and new loot!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/33a482d6a090d4f7da94f9b3eb8d3439590536ef.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/4595a07f37fc54cacff7ef1683bb359948fe0ca6.png[/img]


[h2]Food & Resources[/h2]
[list]
[*] New Food Recipes added to the Kitchenette, offering more buff options.
[*] Mushrooms now spawn in caves, expanding food foraging options.
[*] New Models: Highland Berries & Aloe for better visual distinction.
[*] Cactus now drops Desert Berries and Cactus Flesh, allowing for new food recipes :)
[/list]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/272380a1d99c67e1560e7bcac8254ec586fde5e1.png[/img]

Creatures & Combat[h2]
[/h2]
[list]
[*] New Creature: Desert Metalon – A fierce new enemy found in the desert biome.
[*] Reduced the number of Blue Mecha in the field to two, rebalancing enemy encounters.
[*] Adjusted Blue Mecha Spawn Locations for a more varied experience.
[*] Removed Young Metalons from the spawn area to improve early-game difficulty.
[/list]

[h2]Gameplay & System Changes[/h2]
[list]
[*] New Water System with a more dynamic visual approach.
[*] Fix: Mining helmet flashlight now properly activates.
[*] Changes to Some Recipes for better balance and crafting progression.
[/list]

[h2]
Work in Progress & Upcoming Features[/h2]
While this update brings a ton of new content, we’re also actively working on even bigger additions coming soon!
🔹 Desert Cave Dungeon featuring a Metalon boss and a brand-new Metalon Armor Set. 🔹 Remake of the Field Bunker, adding new challenges and lore. 
🔹 The Tower of the Lost Dungeon in the forest a mysterious new location to explore. 
🔹 Recipe Updates to refine crafting and balance survival mechanics. 
🔹 Building System Update with improved functionality and customization. 
🔹 New Weapons, Tools, and Armors to expand combat and survival strategies.

[h2]Final Notes[/h2]
We appreciate all the feedback from our amazing community as we continue to shape Wild Planet. Keep sharing your discoveries, suggestions, and bug reports. Your support helps us push the game to new heights!

Happy exploring, and watch out for those Metalons!

[b]See you Space Cowboys ! 🚀[/b]

notes.title: Devblog: Shaping the Future of Wild Planet
notes.notes:
Hello, Space Cowboys!

It’s been a busy few weeks for the team as we continue to shape the world of Wild Planet. No many big updates this week but game development often feels like a balancing act between fixing what’s broken, refining what works, and dreaming up new ideas to surprise our players. In this devblog, we’ll take you behind the scenes of our recent work in progress, share some thoughts on our design process, and give you a glimpse of what’s next.

________________________________________
[h1]The Challenges of Co-op Design[/h1][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/28f30aa9db178039681425be63bfb89776b472fd.png[/img]

One of the standout challenges we faced recently was ironing out co-op instancing and interaction bugs. Designing for multiplayer is no small feat. Ensuring that every player sees and interacts with the world in the same way, especially in a dynamic game like ours, is tricky. From syncing objects to handling complex player interactions, it’s a lot like piecing together an intricate puzzle.

We’re happy to report that we’ve solved the core issues, but like all puzzles, there are a few rogue pieces still to fit. A known issue with the unstuck feature and occasional terrain loading hiccups persists. 
________________________________________
[h1]The King Garoo and Expanding the World[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/d39e189317002d5d0c3508c3fae6435796a0637e.png[/img]

We’ve also been diving deep into the Garoo content, designing an all-new Garoo Cave and bringing the King Garoo boss battle to life. Boss fights are a delicate balancing act. They need to be challenging but fair, visually impressive, and rewarding. For King Garoo, we focused on blending its character lore with unique mechanics that feel true to the Wild Planet experience.

And, of course, the King Garoo Suit! When designing rewards like this, we aim for more than just stats—we want players to feel the power and prestige of wearing it. It’s about creating a sense of accomplishment that resonates both in gameplay and in the visual storytelling of your character.
________________________________________
[h1]The Art of Balancing Combat[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/e1bc36c0b5ad25e8321bc63b0771c4d6c0b0ed15.png[/img]

Balancing weapons, armor, and enemies has been another major focus. Combat in Wild Planet is as much about the moment-to-moment excitement as it is about long-term strategy. Every tweak we make—whether it’s adjusting an enemy’s health or fine-tuning a weapon’s damage—has to strike a balance between challenge and fun.

One of our guiding principles here is player agency. Whether you’re taking down a Garoo or battling through a dungeon, your choices should matter. This means ensuring every piece of equipment and every encounter has a purpose, pushing you to adapt and experiment as you progress.
________________________________________
[h1]The Desert: A Realm of Challenge and Discovery[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/0c864ca10f3be6a489eb4079546907e437bc6929.png[/img]

The desert biome is undergoing a major transformation. While this area has always been a place of mystery and harsh survival, we’re now deepening its identity with fresh content and mechanics:

•	Monster Rework: We're reworking the creatures that roam the desert to make them more distinct and thematically tied to the environment. This overhaul includes more dynamic behavior, refined loot tables,  new animations, and improved spawn points that feel natural and enhance exploration. 

•	Resource Overhaul: Gathering resources in the desert will now require strategy and exploration. New resources are being introduced, and their placement will encourage players to engage with the environment in meaningful ways.

•	Desert Bunker Dungeon: We’re hard at work on this new dungeon, which will serve as a key feature of the desert zone. The bunker is a sprawling underground complex filled with secrets, puzzles, and dangers. Designing this space has been a fascinating challenge: How do we contrast the openness of the desert with the claustrophobic, maze-like intensity of the bunker?
________________________________________
[h1]The Forest: A Recycler’s Paradise[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/274f3d3afacd81330b2fdb1b1c94cb1090ab880a.png[/img]

The forest biome is nearing completion, with two major features taking center stage:
•	Recycler Area: This new location will be a hub for turning your scavenged junk into valuable resources. Our goal was to create a mechanic that feels both practical and satisfying, rewarding players for their ingenuity and persistence.
•	Tower of the lost Monument: This larger monument serves as both a landmark and a storytelling piece. Like other monuments in Wild Planet, it combines exploration, lore, and rewards for the curious and determined.
________________________________________
[h1]Building System: Creativity Unleashed[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/4680c2ca134f1cc133213315b58133d2826b7326.png[/img]

We’ve continued refining the building system to meet the expectations of our creative players. Recent updates include bug fixes and the we are working on wall skins and decorations. Whether you’re constructing a rugged desert outpost or a cozy forest hideaway, our goal is to give you the tools to make your base feel like home. Stay stuned more updates and bug fixes are to come.
________________________________________
[h1]Looking Ahead[/h1]
Our roadmap for the next big update is almost ready, and it’s packed with exciting features. Your feedback has been instrumental in shaping Wild Planet, and we’re grateful for every bug report, suggestion, and idea you’ve shared.

Thank you for being part of this journey. As always, see you space cowboys!

— [i][b]Vlad & Yilmaz[/b][/i]

We’re excited to announce that Wild Planet is taking part in Steam Next Fest, and with it, we're bringing a major update to our demo! Version 5.7.0.0 is live, filled with new features, bug fixes, and quality-of-life improvements. Whether you’re revisiting or playing for the first time, there’s plenty to explore.

[h1]What's New in v5.7.0.0?[/h1]
•	Co-op Mode: Team up with a friend! Multiplayer co-op is now available, so you can survive and thrive together on Wild Planet.
•	Female Character: We’ve added a new female character to offer more customization options.
•	New Item - Head Torch: Illuminate your nighttime adventures with the newly added Head Torch.
Major Bug Fixes & Improvements
•	Campfire and Furnace Inventory Fix: We’ve fixed the issue where campfire or furnace inventories would incorrectly appear in storage or workbench inventories.
•	Interaction After Looting: The problem with interactions becoming buggy after looting is now fixed for smoother gameplay.
•	Time Sync: Time and weather sync have been fixed, ensuring that solo and co-op sessions are properly synced. However, time is not yet saved and loaded.
•	UI Updates: Various UI improvements make navigating the game smoother and more intuitive.
•	Customization Fixes: Colors in the customization menu now match exactly as chosen, improving the character creation experience.
•	Mobs and Building Collisions: We’ve improved mob interactions with building structures, making these elements more reliable.
•	Cutout Adjustments: We’ve tweaked how cutouts behave with walls and foundations for better building experiences.
•	Performance Optimizations: Small bug fixes and optimizations ensure the game runs more smoothly.

[h1]Known Bugs in Multiplayer[/h1]
While we’ve made great strides in improving the demo, some known bugs remain in multiplayer:
•	Host-Only Features: Currently, only the host can skip night, enter an instance, or interact with the antenna. We're working on resolving this.
•	Building Restrictions: Players cannot build on foundations they do not own in multiplayer. This will be fixed soon.
•	Desync Issues: Occasionally, desync problems may cause teleportation when entering an instance. Please proceed carefully.
•	Farming Responsiveness: Farming actions can sometimes be a bit unresponsive. We’re aware of this and are working on a fix.

For more details on these bugs, join our Discord to stay up-to-date on progress.

[h1][b]Help Us During Steam Next Fest[/b][/h1]
Even if you've already played the demo, participating during Steam Next Fest will greatly help us gather performance data and feedback. Plus, with co-op mode now live and tons of new features and improvements, it’s the perfect time to dive back into Wild Planet.

notes.title: Devblog: Player Progression & Mechanics
notes.notes:
Welcome back to another devblog update! Today, we're diving into the details of player progression and the core mechanics of our survival open world crafting game. Our goal is to create a gameplay experience that balances survival elements with a chill and accessible vibe. Let's take a closer look at how we've designed our progression system, exploration mechanics, and crafting to ensure an engaging and rewarding experience.

[h2]Survival Elements and Player Progression
[/h2]
Our game is built around key survival elements such as farming, crafting, hunting, and hunger. However, we’ve designed these mechanics to be forgiving and not overly punitive. Our progression curve is designed to be straightforward and enjoyable, avoiding excessive grind while still providing a sense of achievement.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/2e73a2a42119ae66278dc62d64100ac61e107e8a.png[/img]
 
Dungeons also play a crucial role in player progression, offering intense exploration and thrilling boss fights. Each dungeon is meticulously designed to provide unique challenges, requiring players to utilize their skills and resources strategically. As players delve deeper, they encounter formidable bosses, each with distinct abilities and attack patterns. Defeating these bosses not only grants valuable rewards but also unlocks new blueprints for crafting, further enhancing the player's journey. These encounters are crafted to be memorable milestones, testing player progression and offering a deep sense of accomplishment upon victory.
[h2]
Monuments & Exploration
[/h2]
Exploration is a cornerstone of our game, with monument progression mechanisms providing short and medium-term goals. These goals reward players with items that enhance their gameplay experience rather than just offering cosmetic changes. This system is inspired by classic RPGs, giving players multiple options to develop and specialize their characters and bases.
To keep exploration exciting, the entire map isn't accessible from the start. Various mechanisms gradually unlock different areas, encouraging players to discover the world piece by piece. Here’s how we keep exploration engaging:

•	[b]Points of Interest:[/b] We’ve scattered points of interest and resources around the map in clusters to guide players and make exploration rewarding.
•	[b]Topographical Mapping:[/b] The game’s terrain channels player movement, leading them to interesting viewpoints, artifacts, and encounters.
•	[b]Mini-Adventures:[/b] Traveling to a new location becomes a mini-adventure, filled with challenges and discoveries.
•	[b]Biome-Specific Resources:[/b] Certain resources and mobs are unique to specific biomes, linking exploration with tangible rewards.
  
[h2]Crafting & Looting[/h2]

Crafting in our game is more than just a necessity; it’s an integral part of the fun. We’ve designed the crafting system to feel more like building, with various benches and tiers that emphasize player progression and base interaction. Here are the four main points of our crafting system:

1.	[b]Complex Ingredients/Recipes:[/b] Players need to explore the world to gather diverse materials, promoting exploration.
2.	[b]Simple Ingredients/Recipes:[/b] Some recipes require only a few ingredients, focusing on resource management.
3.	[b]Blended Recipes:[/b] A mix of complex and simple recipes ensures players explore and manage resources effectively, fitting seamlessly into the survival gameplay.
4.	[b]Crafting Process:[/b] The crafting process is straightforward; simply clicking on a recipe starts crafting, promoting resource management and multitasking.

Additionally, crafting requires players to follow a progression path. For example, you can’t craft a sword without first crafting a hammer and a furnace. This system provides a clear sense of progression and accomplishment as players unlock new crafting options.

 [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/315de7592bbdd40a57a99fb92406a0998626a622.png[/img]

[h2]Technology Tiers[/h2]
Our technology tiers range from Primitive to Modern, Sci-Fi, and Alien. By starting with familiar, historically-based technology, players can easily understand and adapt to new, more advanced tech as they progress. This gradual introduction ensures an easier learning curve and a sense of continuity. For example, a plasma drill, an evolution of a traditional tool, will intuitively indicate where and how it can be used.

Each technology tier offers tangible rewards and a deep sense of progression through:
•	[b]Visuals:[/b] Distinct visual upgrades reflect technological advancements.
•	[b]Crafting:[/b] New crafting options become available with each tier.
•	[b]Gameplay Upgrades:[/b] Enhanced gameplay mechanics and tools offer new ways to interact with the world.

We believe these elements will provide players with a rich and rewarding experience as they progress through the game.
Stay tuned for more updates, and as always, we appreciate your feedback and support. Happy exploring!

See you Space Cowboys

notes.title: Building the World: Environmental Design in Wild Planet
notes.notes:
Greetings, explorers! Today, we're excited to take you behind the scenes of our game and delve into the intricate process of environmental design and level creation. The world of Wild Planet is vast, diverse, and teeming with life, and we’re thrilled to share how we bring these environments to life, from concept to final design.

[h1]The Vision for Our World[/h1]
Our goal for Wild Planet is to create a world that feels alive and immersive, where every environment tells a story and every level presents unique challenges and experiences. To achieve this, we adhere to several key design principles:

1.	[b]Immersion:[/b] The environments must feel believable and engaging, drawing players into the world.
2.	[b]Exploration:[/b] Each area should encourage players to explore and discover hidden secrets.
3.	[b]Diversity:[/b] Varied biomes and settings to keep the experience fresh and exciting.
4.	[b]Narrative: [/b]Environments should convey the lore and history of the world, adding depth to the gameplay experience.

[h2]Concept Art and Initial Ideas[/h2]
Every great environment starts with a concept. Our artists begin by creating a series of sketches and paintings that capture the essence of each location. These early concepts are crucial for establishing the visual style and mood of the game’s various biomes.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/24ceec55b0b852ecaf8a767db83e3a346cbb484d.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/3906649f06b7031e59ac5fc83af37d617cba1bb2.png[/img]

  
[h2]Level Creation Process[/h2]
Creating these environments is a multi-step process involving collaboration across our entire team. Here’s a glimpse into our level creation process:
The layout of a level is akin to the blueprint of a building. It defines the structure and flow of the player’s journey through the environment.

[h2]Planning the Layout[/h2]
We start by sketching out the level's layout on paper or digital tools. This involves outlining key areas, pathways, points of interest, and objectives. The goal is to create a logical and intuitive path for players to follow while allowing for exploration and discovery.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/85b31b25dd519c525affc219c34008cede745533.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/524d51a1e88291ab0bec02b94a6b21f26eaff149.png[/img]
  
[h3]Key Components[/h3]
•	[b]Main Path:[/b] The primary route that players will take to progress through the level.
•	[b]Secondary Paths:[/b] Optional routes that offer rewards, secrets, or alternative strategies.
•	[b]Points of Interest:[/b] Locations that draw the player’s attention, often containing objectives, lore, or unique encounters.
•	[b]Transitions:[/b] Smooth transitions between different areas to maintain immersion.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/96cdb017de1498cc375a1698d13a00493323a189.png[/img]

Once the layout is established, we move on to designing the level in more detail. This involves creating the environment, populating it with objects and characters, and implementing gameplay mechanics.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/5684d79396224a94e2bc7a0b8b933db6ec623b60.png[/img]
 
[h2]Environmental Storytelling[/h2]
A key aspect of our design is environmental storytelling. We aim to tell stories through the world itself, using visual cues, props, and environmental details. This can include:
•	[b]Visual Landmarks:[/b] Large, noticeable structures that serve as navigation aids and add to the world’s lore.
•	[b]Scattered Details:[/b] Items like abandoned camps, ancient ruins, or fallen trees that hint at past events.
•	[b]Interactive Elements:[/b] Objects that players can interact with to learn more about the world or gain resources.
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/2d7e75d9cf742765148aaf08bd3f21a843365c62.png[/img]

[h2]Balancing Challenge and Flow[/h2]
A well-designed level should challenge players but also allow for moments of relief and exploration. We achieve this balance through:
•	[b]Pacing:[/b] Alternating between intense action sequences and quieter exploration moments.
•	[b]Difficulty Curves:[/b] Gradually increasing the challenge as players progress through the level.
•	[b]Feedback Loops:[/b] Providing immediate feedback to players’ actions, helping them learn and improve.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/5bced24e7ade5d7ef0d37e90b59e27ce5d4cc78b.png[/img]
 
[h2]Logical Design Discussions[/h2]
Behind every level are countless discussions and iterations. Our design team collaborates closely to ensure that each level meets our standards and aligns with the overall vision of the game.
Key Considerations
•	[b]Player Experience:[/b] How does the level make the player feel? Is it engaging and fun?
•	[b]Technical Constraints:[/b] Ensuring the level runs smoothly on all target platforms.
•	[b]Narrative Integration:[/b] Does the level contribute to the overall story and world-building?
•	[b]Replayability:[/b] Are there reasons for players to revisit the level, such as hidden secrets or alternative paths?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/f3e3ba85b296b0ba9135e61b5c7cd12f38e4b2f8.png[/img]
 
[h2]Iterative Process[/h2]
Level design is an iterative process. We create initial versions, playtest them, gather feedback, and make necessary adjustments. This cycle repeats until the level meets our quality standards.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/746adf3d8389961e6d3cc49dba779244aaf80e87.png[/img]
 
[h2]Contribution to Overall Experience[/h2]
The environments in Wild Planet are more than just backdrops—they’re integral to the player experience. Each location is designed to support gameplay mechanics, enrich the narrative, and provide a visually captivating world for players to explore. By combining thoughtful design with detailed execution, we aim to create a world that is both beautiful and engaging, encouraging players to immerse themselves fully in the adventure.

Thank you for joining us on this journey through the environmental design of Wild Planet. We hope you’ve enjoyed this glimpse into our creative process. Stay tuned for more insights and updates, and as always, we welcome your feedback and questions.

Happy exploring! The Wild Planet Team

notes.title: The Artistic Journey of Wild Planet
notes.notes:
Hello, art enthusiasts and fans of Wild Planet! Today, we’re thrilled to take you on a visual journey through the artistic process of our game. From early concept sketches to fully realized environments, the art of wild planet plays a pivotal role in creating an immersive and captivating experience. Let’s dive into the creative process that brings our world to life!

[h2]Setting the Vision: Early Concept Sketches[/h2]

The artistic journey of Wild Planet began with a series of concept sketches that laid the foundation for our game's visual identity. Our lead artist, Yilmaz, started by sketching out initial ideas to explore different styles and themes. These early sketches were crucial in helping us define the overall look and feel of the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/42c34bf396affafa3359d96693f8e6d5da64c475.png[/img]

These sketches were not just random drawings but a carefully crafted exploration of the game’s potential aesthetics. We experimented with various color palettes, architectural styles, and character designs to see what resonated the most with our vision.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/eb5e9bc7a635fe0b70365de13fd43b1fc148358e.png[/img]

[h2]Crafting the Mood: Mood Boards and Inspiration[/h2]

To further refine our artistic direction, we created mood boards that encapsulated the essence of Wild Planet. These boards were filled with images, color swatches, and textures that inspired the team. They served as a visual guide, ensuring that everyone was on the same page regarding the game's atmosphere and setting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/af63eb7f401dcacff3149038be9df2356f022837.png[/img]

Our mood boards drew inspiration from a wide array of sources, including classic scifi literature, historical architecture, and natural landscapes. We wanted the game to have a unique blend of the familiar and the fantastical, creating a world that feels both relatable and otherworldly.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/838dd24d86df01e9574f51316ef686be581122aa.png[/img]

[h2]Building the World: Environmental Design[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/fcd6a3408a2e9540a567788cffddf4ad5584e812.png[/img]

One of the key elements in Wild Planet is its diverse environments. From lush forests to ancient ruins, each location is meticulously designed to enhance the player’s immersion. Our environment 3D artists Yilmaz & Macéo, draws inspiration from real-world landscapes, blending natural beauty with imaginative elements to bring our game’s settings to life. From the dense, mystical forests to the grand, ancient ruins, every location is designed to be visually interesting. 

[h2]Lighting and Color: Setting the Mood[/h2]

Lighting and color play a critical role in establishing the mood of our game. We experimented with different lighting techniques and color schemes to evoke the desired emotions in each scene. Whether it’s the warm glow of a sunset or the eerie shadows of a haunted forest, these elements are essential in immersing players in the game’s atmosphere.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37863626/4ba87f5441179b013d0b93616b2cccdd6ad87c3e.png[/img]

Our technical artist, Vlad, worked closely with the rest of the art team to implement dynamic lighting systems that react to the game’s environments and events. This dynamic approach ensures that each moment in the game feels vibrant and alive.

[h2]Bringing It All Together: The Final Vision[/h2]

The artistic direction of Wild Planet is a culmination of our team's hard work, creativity, and passion. From the earliest sketches to the final in-game assets. We’re incredibly proud of the artistic journey that our game has taken, and we hope that you will feel the same sense of wonder and excitement when you explore our world. The art of Wild Planet is what we define as “minimalism” a mix of minimalist 3D shapes with high fidelity VFX and lighting.

Our ambition has always been to create games with a strong narrative told through the environment. We want players to feel like they've stumbled upon the remnants of an epic battle, piecing together the story from the world around them.

In contrast to the chaos in the world, we aimed to create a colorful, relaxing sci-fi game that offers players a place to unwind. Our core concept revolves around a layered civilization on a random planet.
Our artistic vision led us to a low-poly style, which we believe creates clarity through simplicity. We see low-poly as the gaming equivalent of minimalism. As fans of science fiction, we wanted to merge the genre's complexity with low-poly minimalism to offer a fresh perspective.

Our goal is to give players the freedom to explore and shape the environment in their own way. By leveraging the strengths of the medium, we aim to create in-game narratives without relying on cut-scenes, dialogue, special effects, or complex interfaces.

We embrace minimalism, using simple geometry rendered in high resolution, with flat colors combined with modern shaders featuring specularity and refractions. Good lighting further enhances the visual complexity, proving that simplicity can be stunning.

[h2]Stay Connected[/h2]

We’re excited to share more about the development of Wild planet in the upcoming months. Follow us for the latest updates, behind-the-scenes content, and more. As always, we’d love to hear your thoughts and feedback.

Thank you for joining us on this artistic journey, and we can’t wait for you to experience the world of Wild Planet for yourself!

Until next time,
See you space cowboys.

After a year of navigating through significant challenges and intensive behind-the-scenes efforts, Wild Planet Team is thrilled to announce the early access release of their game on [b]October 23, 2024.[/b] This announcement comes after a period marked by reorganization, changes in game design, and shifting release goals.

[h2]A Rocky Road to Early Access
[/h2]
The past year has been anything but smooth for the Wild Planet Team. The journey began with a substantial investment by publishers, but it soon faced a setback when disagreements led to the loss of those publishers & investment. Despite this, the team was able to secure a small support through state funding and grants, ensuring the continuation of their project.

[h2]Adapting to New Circumstances[/h2]

Given the reduced financing and a downsized team, now consisting of just three dedicated developers , the decision was made to opt for an early access release. This approach allows the team to continue refining and expanding the game with the community's support while securing the necessary resources to move forward.

[h2]What to Expect in Early Access[/h2]

The early access version of the game will feature a vibrant and immersive open world. Players can explore six distinct biomes, covering a large map, filled with multiple dungeons, caves, and dynamic events. The next five months are crucial for further development and polishing, and the team is committed to delivering regular updates and enhancements.

[h2]Community Engagement and Future Plans[/h2]

To maintain transparency and engage with the community, Wild Planet Team will be providing a detailed roadmap and regular development blogs in the coming months. These updates will offer insights into the development process, upcoming features, and improvements.

[h2]Join the Adventure[/h2]

In anticipation of the early access release, a new teaser trailer is now available on the game's Steam page and YouTube channel. Additionally, the team will participate in the [b]Steam Survival Game Festival [/b]starting next week.

[h2]A Heartfelt Thanks[/h2]

The Wild Planet Team extends their deepest gratitude to their supporters and followers. The journey has been challenging, but the unwavering support from the community has been a beacon of hope and motivation. The team is excited to share this milestone and looks forward to the continued journey together.

Stay tuned for more updates and join the adventure on [b]October 23, 2024[/b], as Wild Planet enters its early access phase. Your feedback and support are invaluable as the team strives to create a remarkable gaming experience.

notes.title: Indie Arena Booth 2021
notes.notes:
Hey everyone !
I hope you are doing well !

We will be part of the Swiss Pavilion during Gamescom & Indie Arena Booth 2021. 

Starting from the 25th August until the 29th you will be able to join the indie arena booth for free and visit the expo to discover multiple games (released and not)

But the most important part is that you will be able to join us at the Swissgames booth and cheer for Wild Planet ! 

Maybe we could try to do a screenshot with the booth full of Wild Planet fans screaming "wild planet" in the chat ?`

I'll keep you posted on where we will be on the map and how to join us :slight_smile: 

Be ready to storm Indie Arena Booth Together !

Cheers
Vlad

notes.notes:

Hey there space cowboys ! 

We started writing a new form of "devlog"/"story" about Wild Planet and how it was made, challenges we had to overcome etc.

We are writing the first part on Imgur and we hope we will be able to reach more people and share what it is to be a gamedev.

[url=https://imgur.com/gallery/styoY66]https://imgur.com/gallery/styoY66[/url]

Click this link and if you think it is good, push the upvote button. Doing this helps spread the word and get more people to discover our story & game. 

Thanks to all of you reading us, sometimes it feels like sending a bottle in the ocean but then we have people contacting & supporting us :slight_smile:

Cheers
Vlad & Yilmaz
